title: When reference facts don't cover a claim
statement: Whether a judge given reference facts should fail a claim the facts don't support, or only a claim they contradict.
detail: The AP work's evaluator has two grounding designs that disagree. On an unmerged branch the judge is told that a claim no listed fact supports is unsupported, and the facts are capped at 30 per standard, taken in source-file order with no relevance ranking (`icloud-work/inceptbench/src/inceptbench/evaluators/base.py`). The fact audit and the reference-passage path on the main branch fail only a claim a passage directly contradicts, and say not to penalise correct content a passage doesn't mention (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/tools/factual_accuracy_audit.py`, `icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/question.py`). With the cap, many true claims would have no matching fact, which argues for the contradiction-only reading, but neither reading has been tested.
against: none found; neither reading has been tested.
